correctness.rationale: The published simplex projection formula reduces brightness exactly to the ℓ1 norm of a Haar direction in H0. Represent U as centered iid normal vector Y/||Y||; each coordinate has known sphere-coordinate beta moment and pair Y_i,Y_j correlation −1/(m−1). The exact Gaussian absolute-product identity E|Z1Z2|=(2/π)(sqrt(1−r²)+r arcsin r), together with independence of spherical radius, yields E|UiUj|=(2/(πm))(sqrt(1−r²)+r arcsin r). Summation gives both finite moments; gamma Stirling and Taylor yield the displayed −1/(4πm) variance correction. Centering an iid Gaussian vector changes its ℓ1 norm by O_P(1) and squared radius by O_P(1), hence normalized ℓ1 by o_P(1); the established spherical cube-width CLT or the multivariate delta method gives Gaussian variance 1−3/π. Independently recomputed formula and asymptotic variance corrections at m=3,4,8,100,1000; m×[1−3/π−Var] tends toward 1/(4π). Checked the actual verification script. All-size proof is analytic, not based on simulations.
